items.note: The focused search pill gets a 2px blue border. Results drop into a white rounded menu with a soft float shadow, a result count, and each result's area shown as a hue dot and label. It sits over a yellow hero with a sag arc and a crescent-shaded hexagon cluster. This matches the reference's warm-white-plus-field language (01/02). The menu is plain, with no highlighted first result, but it reads clearly.

Night version: the search pill has a yellow ring and the results menu is an indigo panel with hue dots. The yellow hero keeps its hue over a navy page, as the derived night palette intends (03). The full page still ends in a bright white bottom bar under the indigo footer.

On the phone the search pill spans the width and has a blue focus border. A white floating results card with hue-dot area labels overlays the stacked, centred yellow hero, which has full-width pills and a compact cluster below, close to the reference phone (04). The results are large and easy to tap.

The no-match menu shows '0 results', a helpful line about the query, and three yellow dots as its only art. The dots are the system's loading glyph, so the state looks half like 'still searching'. There is no next step such as a link to browse the docs. The reference's spot pictograms (07) would draw the subject instead.

Same as light on an indigo menu: three yellow loader-style dots beside the no-results text and no follow-up action. The night colours are right, but the state reads as loading rather than as a designed empty state.

Phone: a white card with '0 results', the three-dot loader glyph and two lines of advice over the yellow hero. The text is large and clear, but the art says 'loading' and the card offers no way forward.

The cream sidebar shows one group collapsed with a right chevron while the others stay open. The current page is an ink pill with a white dot (09's active tab). Area-hue dots mark each group, and a blue header band with a sag arc and a disc-and-pill cluster sits beside it. The state is clear and in the system's language.

Night: an indigo sidebar, with the current page as a white pill with an ink dot and the collapsed group's chevron clear. The blue header band and its cluster are unchanged on navy. This is a faithful translation of the night palette.

Code sits in cream rounded blocks with a white 'Copy' pill. After a click it turns into a pill with a green tick and 'Copied', following the spec's tick-for-success. Package-manager tabs use the ink pill with dot. The feedback is small but unambiguous and in the system's language.

Night version of the same page: indigo code blocks and a table-of-contents panel, the selected tab as a white pill, and the blue header band on navy. The copied pill keeps its tick. It is consistent with the light state and with 03's night palette.

On the phone the compact blue header band has a corner cluster and the breadcrumb wraps under it. A cream 'On this page' panel follows, and the copied pill with its green tick shows on the first code block. Long code lines scroll inside their frame. The band is compact and the state is easy to read.

Keyboard focus lands on the search pill, whose border turns 2px blue, as the spec asks for inputs. The rest of the first screen is the strong yellow hero with crescent-shaded art. The focus is clearly visible and fits the reference's blue-ring state (11).
Night: the focused search pill gets a yellow border on the navy bar. It is clearly visible and matches the on-dark ring logic, with the hero unchanged.

Focus is on the wordmark link and shows as a flush, square-cornered blue box hugging the text. Every pill in the system instead gets the rounded ring offset by 2px seen in the reference (11), so this focus looks like a browser default rather than the system's.

A cream drawer slides over a dimmed page. It has an ink 'Close' pill on its ledge, area-hue dots per item, the current page as a full-width ink pill with a white dot, and bold group labels with chevrons. Large rows and a clear exit match the reference's pill and dot vocabulary (09/10).

The hero cluster has a crescent-shaded hexagon overlapped by a shaded orange disc, a flat-bottomed cloud and two sparkle sizes, built to the recipe. The section covers are a sun over a hill, an open book, a plug and a lightbulb, each on its area hue with a sparkle, plus a stopwatch on a cream plate and a two-colour confetti disc. Each reads as its subject and is its own drawing, at a flatness and scale close to 07. The book and lightbulb lack the crescent shading.

The header cluster is a shaded yellow disc overlapped by a green pill with two sparkles. It is well built but says nothing about its page. The four small glyphs on the helpful/previous/next controls are a crescent with a sparkle, two bubbles, a ring and a zigzag, assigned with no tie to their labels. The reference (05) picks each row's glyph for its label.

The header cluster is a tilted yellow pill overlapped by a pink disc with sparkles. It is cleanly shaded but generic, and near the installation page's disc-plus-pill layout. The same four arbitrary glyphs repeat on the footer controls, recoloured green, so a hue swap stands in for a new drawing.

The pink header band holds a flat-bottomed white cloud in front of a crescent-shaded yellow sun, with a large blue and a small violet sparkle. It is a tight, well-proportioned cluster that reads like 02's cloud-and-sparkle accents, and it differs from the other areas' lead shapes.

Hero text and art fade in once. Section confetti and the two-colour disc fade in staggered, one disc drifts slowly, and the small ring glyphs breathe on slow scale cycles. Nothing bounces or slides far. This matches the spec's calm reveal-and-breathe motion and the reference's slow breathing glyphs.

findings.summary: The no-results search state uses three yellow dots, the system's own loading glyph, as its only art, and offers no next step. A person can mistake 'nothing found' for 'still loading' and is left with nowhere to go. The reference states outcomes with a pictogram of the subject (07). Earlier rounds named weak no-results art, and the agent again picked a dots glyph that the spec lists among its glyph forms.
findings.promptFix: The three-dot glyph means loading and nothing else. An empty or no-results state, even inside a compact menu or popover, shows a crescent-shaded pictogram of what was looked for (for example a magnifier, or the area's subject) or a different glyph that is not the loader. It always offers one next step: a link or pill to clear the query or browse.

findings.summary: In dark mode the page still ends in a bright white bottom bar under the indigo footer, the one element that breaks the night palette. This was flagged in rc.3 and is unchanged.
findings.promptFix: Give the footer's bottom bar its own token that stays dark at night (the night page or a deeper navy, with white text), rather than `surface.inverse`, which flips to white in the dark theme.
findings.specRule: Footer: "`surface.inverse` bottom bar with round icon buttons"; dark token table: "`color.surface.inverse` | `#ffffff`"

findings.summary: Keyboard focus on a text link (the wordmark) is a flush, square-cornered box hugging the glyphs. The reference's focus is a rounded ring offset 2px (11), and every pill here gets it, so text-link focus looks like a browser default. This is still open since rc.2.

Small glyphs on the page-footer controls (helpful yes/no, previous/next) are the generic crescent, bubbles, ring and zigzag, assigned with no tie to their labels and repeated on every page in a new hue. Header-band clusters on two guide pages are near-mirrored disc-and-pill pairs that do not speak to the page subject. The reference picks each glyph for its label (05).
